modules.name: Anime reactions
modules.summary: Drops an anime reaction picture when someone says your trigger words, or mentions a mood. You set the words, the chance and the mode.
modules.description:
Reactions without any reaction service: the bot decides in Python. Write your own trigger words and phrases per category (one line each, like “happy@80: yay, good news”, where @80 is that line's own chance), or switch on the general mode, where mentioning a mood (sad, thinking, surprised, dance, lunch…) is enough. Pick words, category or both, set how likely a trigger is to fire, the cooldown per channel, which categories and channels are allowed, and whether the bot replies or just posts.

15 categories: angry, calm-down, confused, dance, embarrassed-nervous, happy, lunch-break-time, misc, no, pre-exercise, sad, smug, surprised, thinking, yes. Commands: !react [category], !reactions, and for owners !reactadd and !reactremove.

The pictures aren't inside this module: 300+ reaction pictures, all optimized to 512×512 and under 1 MB, are downloaded once from this marketplace when first needed and cached. You can also use your own folder (data/reactions/images/<category>/, or another folder in Settings). The pictures come from the shadorki/anime-reaction-api collection and belong to their artists. This module runs Python, so it needs Settings → Marketplace → Allow modules with code.
modules.author: lucky-edgelord

modules.name: Fable
modules.summary: A Mudae-style character gacha: !roll anime characters, react to claim them, then collect, wish, trade, steal and merge.
modules.description:
Fable is a character-collecting game, in the style of Mudae and the Fable bot. Type !roll and a random anime character appears with a rating from 1 to 5 stars (odds 50/30/15/4/1 percent). React with the claim emoji, or type !claim, and the first person to do so takes the character home. Everyone gets an hourly allowance of rolls and one claim every few hours. Each character belongs to one person per community.

Collect with !harem, look characters up with !im, and !wish for the ones you want so you get first pick when they appear. Put favourites in your !party. !givechar and !trade move characters between people (the other person confirms with a reaction). !steal tries to take one from someone, with a chance set by its rating that grows when the owner has been away. !merge turns five characters of one rating into one of the next. !divorce releases a character for coins. Coins are the bot's own wallet (!bal, !daily), so they're the same coins as the rest of Vectiq; !fshop sells roll resets and guaranteed high-rating pulls (!fbuy). !tu shows your rolls and cooldowns.

The 2,500 characters were collected from AniList when the module was built; nothing calls an API while playing except downloading each picture once (kept afterwards). Everything is adjustable: rolls per hour, claim cooldown and window, channels, and which features are allowed. This module runs Python, so it needs Settings → Marketplace → Allow modules with code. Cards are drawn from AniList's character pictures, which belong to their rights holders.

modules.name: Kitsune
modules.summary: The Fox Mafia's anime fox-girl: !kit chats in text, !kitsune answers in a lip-synced talking video with subtitles.
modules.description:
Kitsune is the bot from the Kitsune repository, as a module. Talk to her with !kit and she answers in text, or with !kitsune and she answers in a short video: her avatar lip-syncs to a NovelAI voice, blinks, and shows one of five moods (happy, mad, neutral, sad, shy) picked from what she says, with subtitles burned in. Her mood also appears as a reaction on your message. Reply to any of her answers to keep talking, in the same mode. She remembers each person (!kitmemory, !kitforget), summarising old chats into notes, and 👍/👎 votes on her answers are kept. !kitface shows an expression. Owners can give the bot her name and picture with !kitprofile, or the button on her dashboard page. List channels under “Chat in these channels” and she answers every message there, no command needed.

Needs: an Ollama API key (ollama.com, free tier works) in the bot's .env as OLLAMA_API_KEY, or a local Ollama. For videos: ffmpeg, a NovelAI token in .env as NOVELAI_TOKEN for her voice, and the Python packages numpy and httpx (the one-line Vectiq installer adds them; on older installs run pip install numpy httpx). Without those she still answers in text. This module runs Python, so it needs Settings → Marketplace → Allow modules with code. Her 20 sprite frames (the Fox Mafia's art, 512×512) are downloaded from this marketplace the first time she needs them and kept.
modules.author: lucky-edgelord

modules.name: Visual Novel
modules.summary: Talk with Gwen, an AI visual-novel character who answers as a scene: her expression, where you are, her line in the dialogue box.
modules.description:
Visual Novel turns chat into a visual novel. Type !vn and a message, and Gwen answers with a scene: one of her 11 expressions, picked by the AI to match what she says, in one of 7 places (bridge, swing, grove, path, greenhouse, house, table), with her line in the dialogue box. The same line is in the message as text, so it's easy to read on a phone. Reply to her scene to keep talking. Long answers get ◀️ ▶️ page reactions, and 🗺️ opens the map: react 1-7 to walk somewhere together, or use !vngo grove. Everyone has their own scene and conversation. !vnreset makes her forget yours, and !vnface shows an expression. List channels under "Chat in these channels" and she answers every message there, no command needed. Change her name and personality in the settings to make her someone else.

Needs an Ollama API key (ollama.com, free tier works) in the bot's .env as OLLAMA_API_KEY, or a local Ollama. Her pictures (about 1.4 MB) are downloaded from this marketplace the first time she's needed and kept. This module runs Python, so it needs Settings → Marketplace → Allow modules with code. Rewritten from atorsvn/visual_novel_chat_poc.

modules.name: Run code
modules.summary: !run code in 80+ languages right in chat, on a Piston server. Edit your message to run it again.
modules.description:
Run code is engineer-man's piston-bot for Vectiq. Type !run and a language, then your code in a code block, and the bot answers with the output, the exit code and how long it took. Lines between the command and the block are command-line arguments; lines after it are standard input. You can attach a source file instead (the extension picks the language), or reply !run to someone's message that has a code block. C, C++, Go, Java, Rust, Scala and C# get their main() added when you leave it out. Edit your message and the answer updates; delete it and the answer goes too. !langs lists the languages, !rundel removes your last answer. Output is limited to 30 lines, and each person gets a few runs a minute.

The code runs on a Piston server, never on the bot's computer. Piston's public server has been whitelist-only since February 2026, so run your own: docker run -d --privileged -p 2000:2000 ghcr.io/engineer-man/piston, install the languages you want with its CLI, then set Piston server to http://localhost:2000/api/v2/piston. If you have a whitelisted key, put it in .env as PISTON_API_KEY. This module runs Python, so it needs Settings → Marketplace → Allow modules with code.
modules.author: engineer-man, lucky-edgelord
